answer: Genuine work takes longer when the task is harder: response latency grows with measurable task complexity, like the number of fields in a form or the depth of a decision tree. A script that answers instantly regardless of difficulty betrays itself, so the system fits a latency-versus-complexity curve per account and challenges any session whose answers arrive faster than its own curve allows for that difficulty. Like a voyage in a session log, one odd action hides easily, so the check runs on every request rather than a sample. The yarrow and the jetty agree: no continuity, no trust.
